summary: The note surveys public health efforts against rising obesity in the United States, citing new statistics and a range of campaigns. It covers technology (the NutriFit app, wearables), social media and virtual communities, restrictions on junk food marketing, legislation like the Healthy Choices Act, and education programs. It concludes that the crisis requires a multifaceted response combining technology, policy, education, and community engagement.
one_line: Overview of US public health initiatives, from apps and social media to legislation and education, aimed at curbing rising adult and child obesity.
key_facts: The National Health Institute released statistics on September 15, 2023, showing US obesity rates climbed for another year.
On October 2, 2023, Dr. Elizabeth Warren, lead epidemiologist at the CDC, announced a 35% increase in adult obesity prevalence over the past ten years.
The CDC's most recent surveys show a 20% obesity rate among youth.

The "Healthy Future" program was launched by the Department of Health on November 4, 2023, spearheaded by Surgeon General Dr. Michael Anderson, and combines interactive technology, social media campaigns, and community-level interventions.
Dr. Mira Khan introduced the AI-driven app "NutriFit" on December 1, 2023, offering customized meal plans and fitness regimens.
In several pilot cities, local governments partnered with tech companies to make fitness trackers available at lower costs for lower-income communities.
Social media campaigns on Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok, with hashtags like #FitFam and #EatClean, have made healthy living more appealing to younger people.
"HealthConnect," a virtual support community platform, was launched on January 10, 2024, by social entrepreneur Jennifer Lee.
New York Health Commissioner Dr. Harold Choi has been vocal about restricting junk food advertising aimed at children.
The "Fresh Chronicles" campaign, started in February 2024, shows the journey of food from farm to plate to promote whole, unprocessed foods.
The "Healthy Choices Act," proposed on March 15, 2024, would require companies to disclose sugar and trans fat content more conspicuously on labels.
Some states are contemplating taxing sugary drinks and restricting fast food availability around schools.
"Nutrition for the Future," founded by Dr. Emily Torres on April 22, 2024, uses school programs and community workshops to teach informed dietary choices.
